title: Free Variables and the Shape of the Solution Set
quickIdea: A consistent system with rank r in n unknowns has n - r free parameters. Its solutions are one particular solution plus every solution of Ax = 0, so the set is a point, a line, a plane or a higher-dimensional flat, never a finite cluster.
remember: Pivot columns correspond to basic variables; the remaining n - r columns are free, and each free variable contributes one parameter.
Every solution is x = x_p + x_n, where x_p is any one solution of Ax = b and x_n runs over the null space of A, that is over all solutions of Ax = 0.
The number of parameters is n - rank(A), which is the nullity. It does not depend on b.
Consequently a consistent system has 1 solution when rank(A) = n, and infinitely many when rank(A) < n. There is no third possibility.
If two different solutions exist, infinitely many exist: their difference is a non-zero null vector, and every multiple of it can be added to either solution.

example.prompt: Describe all solutions of x + y + z = 3 and x - y = 0.
example.work: A = [[1,1,1],[1,-1,0]] has rank 2 in n = 3 unknowns, so there is 3 - 2 = 1 free parameter. Take z = t: then x = y from the second equation, and 2x + t = 3 gives x = y = (3 - t)/2. So the solutions are ((3-t)/2, (3-t)/2, t) for every real t.
example.answer: A one-parameter family: a line in R^3. One particular solution is (3/2, 3/2, 0), and the null space is spanned by (-1/2, -1/2, 1).

gateAngle: GATE CSE 2024 Set 1 Q.39 is entirely about this bookkeeping: for an n x m matrix with m > n the nullity is at least m - n, so at least that many independent solutions of Ax = 0 exist. GATE CSE 2021 Set 2 Q.24 is the same count read backwards, from a one-dimensional null space to rank 4.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: A is 4 x 5 and the system Ax = b is consistent with rank(A) = 4. How many solutions are there?
variations.answer: Infinitely many, forming a one-parameter family.
variations.why: The nullity is 5 - 4 = 1, so the solution set is a line: a particular solution plus all multiples of one null vector.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: A 3 x 3 system has exactly two solutions, (1,0,0) and (0,1,0). Is that possible?
variations.answer: No. Two solutions force infinitely many.
variations.why: Their difference (1,-1,0) is a non-zero null vector, so (1,0,0) + t(1,-1,0) solves the system for every real t.

trap.what: Reporting 'no solution or one solution or two solutions' as the possibilities, or assuming the number of solutions can be counted when the determinant vanishes.
trap.why: The solution set of a consistent linear system is an affine subspace. Its size is 1 or infinite, and the only question is how many parameters it has.
trap.counterexample: x + y = 2 and 2x + 2y = 4 have the solutions (2 - t, t) for every real t; no choice of b makes this system have exactly two solutions.

check.question: A is 3 x 5 with rank 3 and Ax = b is consistent. How many parameters does the solution set have?
check.explanation: The nullity is n - rank = 5 - 3 = 2, so two free variables remain and the solution set is a plane inside R^5.
